item.title: D.League: Japan’s Pro Dance League Live at Toyota Arena Tokyo
item.dc:creator: TC Team
item.description:
Japan’s professional dance league brings two nights of crew-versus-crew battles to Toyota Arena Tokyo in Odaiba on December 10 and 11, 2026, with shows starting at 6:30 p.m. What to expect Founded in 2020, D.League bills itself as the world’s biggest professional dance competition. Its 20 teams compete across two divisions, Block Hype and Block Vibe, over the season for one of six spots in the D.League Championship. Each competition night features five matches, plus halftime performances you can only see at the venue. It’s a family-friendly show, so dance fans of all ages are welcome. item.title: Sanrio Puroland Christmas
item.dc:creator: TC Team
item.description:
Help Santa get ready for the holiday season at Sanrio Puroland’s Christmas event. What to expect The headliner is Sweet Sparkle Illumination, a new 10-minute light-and-laser show in Puro Village on the first floor. Show times change daily, so check the schedule. It’s also Puroland’s first tie-in with Kuma no Gakkō (The Bears’ School), the picture-book series about a little bear called Jackie. There’s a free four-stop stamp rally with a star-shaped card at the end, story readings in the Entertainment Hall, and Jackie herself appears before the parade on November 21 and 22 and December 19 and 20. item.title: Hagiyama Park Autumn Leaves Light-Up
item.dc:creator: TC Team
item.description:
Out in Kodaira, a neighborhood park with more than 100 Japanese maples gets lit up after dark for a couple of weeks, and it costs nothing to walk through. What to expect Hagiyama Park has no streetlights to speak of, which is the whole point: the lit-up iroha momiji seem to float out of the darkness, and it does feel more immersive than the big-name gardens where you shuffle along a roped path. There are no food trucks this year because of renovation work in the park, so grab a hot drink near the station on your way. |credit| Schedule Saturday, November 28 to Sunday, December 13, 2026, lit from 5:30 p.m. to 8:30 p.m. every evening. item.title: Yakiimo Fes Tokyo 2027
item.dc:creator: TC Team
item.description:
Ten days of yakiimo (roasted sweet potato) in every form you can think of, and a few you probably can’t. Yakiimo Fes Tokyo takes over the event area of Nakano Shiki no Mori Park every autumn. What to expect The festival brings together sweet potato specialists from all over Japan. In 2026, 14 of them (from Ibaraki and Saitama to Kyoto and Miyazaki) set up stalls with around 30 dishes between them. There’s plenty of plain, honest yakiimo, like tasting flights of different varieties, alongside more inventive creations such as sweet potato fries, crisp-shelled chocolate sweet potato, aged sweet potato sticks, and a sweet potato smothered in honey and molten cheese. Honey and cheese yakiimo, one of the 2026 festival dishes.|credit|
